title: Buddy Petit's illness and death across the lake
summary: Petit lost his health to tuberculosis across Lake Pontchartrain and died there; Bigard only played jobs with him there.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: The drummer would be right up near the driver then, the front end of the truck? Yes. The bass player would be on the end. Back at the tailgate. Yeah, tailgate. Him and the tri-roll. I was going to ask. Some more about Buddy Petit. The other night we talked to Sammy Penn, the drummer who used to play with him too. He talked like Buddy lived across the lake at the end of his life. Do you remember those days? Did he ever talk about going across the lake much? Buddy did go across the lake. He lost his health. That's where he lost his health. He went to TB. I didn't know he had TB. And he died. He looked pretty small anyway, didn't he? He died across the lake. He died over there then. Did any of his old man Joe Petit, I knew the trombonist, his stepfather, he never lived over there though, did he? No. I thought maybe Buddy, Sammy talked like his family lived over there or something. I didn't know what he meant though, by his family. Did he have a wife over there maybe or something? Do you know? I don't know. I couldn't tell you whether he went to live over there after that. You weren't with him in those days. You never worked across the lake then with him? Oh yeah, I went across the lake with him. Not there. I used to go to Pugaloosa. Just there wasn't a job though. You didn't go over there like all summer to stay there. Oh no, no, no, no, no, no, no. That's what I wondered. Just jobs.
Yeah. I was wondering about him now. I was asking you before. Could he stay out for a whole mamba and keep punching on him? Oh yeah, yeah. He was that strong, huh? That's right. That's right.
